result.rationale: The diff defines `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Zod schema objects have no custom toString, so both keys evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a dynamic property matcher. The schema therefore only enforces `access_token: z.string()` plus an "[object Object]" field, contradicting the comment 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry'. It's also used for the refresh_token falsy check — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` will never exist, so it always defaults to "refresh_token"

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a string (likely "[object Object]"), not treated as a pattern for arbitrary keys, so the schema does not enforce “any numeric property” for expiry as the comment claims. This affects the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT path where this schema is used for safeParse, weakening/incorrectly defining validation for token refresh responses.
